title: Adding transaction savepoints interpolated the caller-supplied savepoint name into SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE statements with f-strings.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: User-controlled savepoint name is directly interpolated into SQL query using f-string without parameterization. The 'name' parameter comes from user input (either passed directly or generated, but still under user control via the savepoint() method). SQL injection is possible if an attacker provides a malicious savepoint name.

Identical SQL injection vulnerability in SQLite implementation. User-controlled savepoint name is directly interpolated into SQL queries using f-strings without parameterization in rollback_to(), release(), and savepoint() methods.

findings.explanation: User-controlled savepoint name is directly interpolated into SQL query using f-string without parameterization. The 'name' parameter comes from user input (either passed directly or generated, but still under user control via the savepoint() method). evidence.content:
async def rollback_to(self):
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

async def release(self):
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"RELEASE SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

async def savepoint(self, name: t.Optional[str] = None) -> Savepoint:
        name = name or f"savepoint_{self.get_savepoint_id()}"
        await self.connection.execute(f"SAVEPOINT {name}")

findings.suggested_fix: Use parameterized queries or strict allowlisting for savepoint names. PostgreSQL doesn't support parameterized identifiers directly, so use a whitelist of allowed characters or a generated safe format. Example: validate that savepoint names match pattern `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` or use identifier escaping if the driver supports it.

findings.explanation: No authorization checks are introduced or modified. The nested transaction feature is an internal transaction management mechanism that operates within the context of the same database connection established during outer transaction entry. There is no object fetching by user-controlled ID or cross-tenant access scenarios.
